hook: The sound that makes you|*see ghosts*

lines.say: In the 1980s, an engineer named Vic Tandy worked in a lab in England that people said was haunted.
shots: q: old industrial lab building England night

lines.say: One night, he felt cold, uneasy, and saw a grey shape at the edge of his vision. When he turned to look, it was gone.
shots: q: blurred shadow corner dark room

lines.say: The next day he was fixing a fencing sword in a vise, and the blade started vibrating on its own.
He traced it to a new extractor fan. It was producing sound at nineteen cycles a second. Too low for humans to hear.
shots: line art: sound wave 19 Hz below hearing line

lines.say: When the fan was fixed, the feeling, and the ghost, disappeared.
Low sound like this, called infrasound, has been linked in some experiments to anxiety, chills and a sense of presence, and may even make the eyeball vibrate slightly.
shots: line art: eye outline with vibration lines

lines.say: Not every haunting is a fan. But some of them might be.

fact_note: Tandy & Lawrence, 'The Ghost in the Machine', J. Society for Psychical Research 1998 (KNOWN). 18.98 Hz fan, fencing foil (KNOWN). Eyeball resonance ~18 Hz claim from NASA-era studies (DEBATED). 2003 concert infrasound experiment (Wiseman/Lord) found more unusual feelings (KNOWN, small study).
ig_caption: a guy saw a ghost in his lab and it turned out to be a fan. a literal fan. still one of my favorite stories
tt_caption: infrasound, the 19 Hz frequency linked to ghost sightings #ghosts #science

lines.say: In 1921, an eye doctor published a strange case in the American Journal of Ophthalmology.
A family, called only Mr. and Mrs. H, had moved into an old house. And things started happening.
shots: q: old Victorian house exterior dusk

lines.say: They heard bells ringing at night. Footsteps. Furniture moving. They felt invisible hands. They saw figures in the rooms.
shots: q: chair in empty room shadow

lines.say: They also had constant headaches. They felt weak. The plants in the house were dying.
Then they found the cause. The furnace was broken, and it was leaking carbon monoxide.
Carbon monoxide has no smell and no color. In low doses it can cause headaches, confusion, and hallucinations.
shots: q: invisible gas haze light beam

lines.say: Once the furnace was fixed, the ghosts left. If your house feels haunted, check your detector first.
shots: q: sunlight in old house window

fact_note: W. H. Wilmer, 'Effects of carbon monoxide upon the eye', American Journal of Ophthalmology 1921, case of 'Mr. and Mrs. H' (KNOWN). Symptoms incl. bells, footsteps, figures, headaches, dying plants (KNOWN as reported). CO causes hallucinations in some cases (KNOWN).
ig_caption: bells, footsteps, figures... and a broken furnace. please check your CO detector lol
tt_caption: the 1921 haunted house that was carbon monoxide poisoning #haunted #creepyhistory

hook: The two girls who|*started* talking to the dead

lines.say: March 1848. Hydesville, New York. Two sisters, Maggie and Kate Fox, say they're hearing knocks in their house at night.
shots: line art: knocking sound waves on wall

lines.say: They start asking the knocks questions. The knocks answer. One knock for yes. Silence for no.
The story explodes. Within a few years, a whole movement called Spiritualism has grown across America and Britain, with mediums and séances everywhere.
Then in 1888, forty years later, Maggie stands on a stage in New York and confesses.
The knocks were made by cracking the joints of her toes. She demonstrated it in front of the audience.
shots: line art: foot outline, joint highlighted

lines.say: A year later, she took the confession back. By then it didn't matter. Spiritualism no longer needed the Fox sisters.
A movement with millions of followers may have started with two girls playing a trick that got out of hand.

fact_note: Hydesville, 31 March 1848 (KNOWN). Spiritualism spread rapidly (KNOWN). Margaret's public confession and toe-joint demonstration, New York Academy of Music, Oct 1888 (KNOWN). Recantation 1889 (KNOWN). Whether all phenomena were trickery is the DEBATED part.
ig_caption: a whole religious movement may have started with two kids cracking their toes. and she showed everyone how on stage
tt_caption: the Fox sisters and the birth of Spiritualism #spiritualism #ghosthistory

lines.say: This is Mary Todd Lincoln, years after her husband was assassinated.
shots: archive: Mumler photo Mary Todd Lincoln (public domain), full
archive: same photo slow push on face

lines.say: Behind her, with his hands on her shoulders, is a pale figure that looks a lot like Abraham Lincoln.
shots: archive: same photo, push on hands
line art: outline tracing the figure

lines.say: It was taken by William Mumler, a Boston engraver who became famous in the 1860s for spirit photography.
shots: archive: Mumler spirit photographs collage (public domain)

lines.say: A few years earlier he'd been put on trial in New York for fraud. Some of his ghosts were recognized as living people from Boston.
P.T. Barnum, the showman, testified against him. Mumler was acquitted anyway, for lack of proof of how he did it.
Today we know the method: a double exposure, two images on one glass plate.
Mary may have known, or not. She wanted to see him one more time. That's what she paid for.
shots: archive: Mumler photo crop on her face

fact_note: Mumler photo of Mary Todd Lincoln c. 1872 (KNOWN, public domain). Mumler first spirit photo 1861-62 Boston (KNOWN). 1869 New York fraud trial, Barnum testified, acquitted (KNOWN). Living 'ghosts' recognized (KNOWN as reported). Double exposure method (KNOWN consensus).
ig_caption: I can't look at this photo without feeling sad. whatever it was, she wanted to see him again
tt_caption: the ghost of Abraham Lincoln photo, and the man who faked it #lincoln #spiritphotography

lines.say: September 1936. Two photographers are shooting a magazine story at Raynham Hall, an old English country house.
shots: q: English country house Norfolk exterior || alt: English country house rural English exterior

lines.say: One of them suddenly shouts: there's something on the staircase. The other takes the shot.
When the negative was developed, there was a pale, veiled figure coming down the stairs.
shots: line art: redraw of staircase with veiled figure (check licence of original)

lines.say: Locals said it was the Brown Lady, the ghost of Lady Dorothy Walpole, who died in that house in 1726.
shots: archive: 18th c. portrait of a lady (public domain)

lines.say: The magazine Country Life published it in December 1936, and it has been reprinted ever since.
shots: q: dust in light old library

lines.say: Skeptics point to a double exposure, or a smudge on the lens, or a figure placed on the stairs. Experts who examined the negative at the time found no sign of tampering.
Nearly ninety years later, nobody has proven how it was made.

fact_note: Photographed by Capt. Hubert Provand and Indre Shira, Sept 1936; published Country Life 26 Dec 1936 (KNOWN). Brown Lady identified with Lady Dorothy Walpole d. 1726 (KNOWN legend). Explanations (DEBATED). LICENCE: 1936 UK photo may still be in copyright; use a line-art redraw unless TTB confirms PD.
ig_caption: this photo is almost 90 years old and people still fight about it. I zoomed in way too long
tt_caption: the Brown Lady of Raynham Hall, the most famous ghost photo #ghostphoto #paranormal

lines.say: This painting is called The Nightmare. Henry Fuseli, 1781.
shots: archive: Fuseli The Nightmare 1781 (public domain), full

lines.say: A woman lies asleep, twisted across the bed. On her chest sits a demon, staring straight at us.
For centuries people described exactly this. Waking up, unable to move, with something heavy sitting on your chest, and a presence in the room.
In Newfoundland they called it the Old Hag. In other places, a witch, a jinn, a spirit.
shots: q: Newfoundland coast night || alt: rugged north Atlantic coast night

lines.say: Science calls it sleep paralysis. Your brain wakes up while your body is still locked in dream sleep, and the dream bleeds into the room.
shots: line art: brain awake, body asleep

lines.say: Studies suggest something like one person in twelve has it at least once.
So that demon on her chest? People really saw it. It just came from inside their own heads.
shots: archive: Nightmare crop on demon eyes

fact_note: Fuseli 'The Nightmare' 1781, Detroit Institute of Arts (KNOWN, PD). Old Hag (Newfoundland) and other cultural names (KNOWN). REM atonia intrusion into wakefulness (KNOWN). Lifetime prevalence ~7.6% general population (Sharpless & Barber 2011) (KNOWN; 'one in twelve').
ig_caption: had sleep paralysis twice in my life and this painting is EXACTLY it
tt_caption: sleep paralysis and the demon on your chest #sleepparalysis #fuseli

hook: A Roman ghost story|that *ends* with bones

lines.say: Almost two thousand years ago, a Roman writer named Pliny the Younger wrote a letter asking a friend: do ghosts exist?
shots: archive: Pliny the Younger statue Como (public domain photo)
q: Roman letter wax tablet stylus

lines.say: Then he tells a story. In Athens there was a big house nobody would live in.
At night you'd hear chains. Then an old man would appear, thin, filthy, with chains on his legs and wrists, rattling them.
A philosopher named Athenodorus rented it anyway, because it was cheap. He sat up writing. The ghost came. It beckoned. He followed it into the courtyard, where it vanished.
shots: q: oil lamp writing desk night

lines.say: He marked the spot with leaves. The next day he had it dug up.
They found bones, tangled in chains. They gave them a proper burial. And the haunting stopped.
shots: q: old bones in soil archaeology

lines.say: The chained ghost, the unburied body, the haunting that ends with a burial. Ghost stories have barely changed since.

fact_note: Pliny the Younger, Letters 7.27 to Licinius Sura (KNOWN), c. AD 100. Athenodorus, chained ghost, leaves as marker, bones in chains, burial ends haunting (KNOWN).
ig_caption: this is basically every haunted house movie, written down around the year 100
tt_caption: the oldest haunted house story, from ancient Rome #ghoststory #ancientrome

lines.say: Harry Houdini spent his last years exposing fake mediums. He knew every trick because he did them on stage.
But he never said contact with the dead was impossible. So he made a deal with his wife, Bess.
shots: archive: Harry and Bess Houdini photo (public domain)

lines.say: Whoever died first would try to send back a secret message. A code only the two of them knew.
Houdini died on Halloween, 1926. For ten years, Bess held a séance every Halloween.
Mediums claimed to have the message. None convinced her for good.
The last official séance was on Halloween 1936, on a hotel rooftop in Hollywood, broadcast on the radio. Nothing came through.
shots: q: Hollywood night 1930s archive || alt: city night 1930s archive

lines.say: Bess turned off the candle and said: ten years is long enough to wait for any man. The code, published later, was Rosabelle, believe.

fact_note: Houdini's anti-medium campaign, A Magician Among the Spirits 1924 (KNOWN). Died 31 Oct 1926 (KNOWN). Code pact with Bess; 'Rosabelle, believe' (KNOWN). Arthur Ford 1929 claim (DEBATED, not mentioned in detail). Final séance 31 Oct 1936, Knickerbocker Hotel roof, radio broadcast, 'Ten years is long enough to wait for any man' (KNOWN).
ig_caption: 'ten years is long enough to wait for any man'. Bess Houdini is the main character of this story honestly
tt_caption: Houdini's secret code to prove the afterlife #houdini #afterlife

lines.say: Ghosts change with the times. Watch.
Around the year 100, Roman ghosts were thin old men in chains, asking for a proper burial.
Medieval England had revenants: not see-through spirits, but actual corpses walking out of graves. Chroniclers wrote of villagers digging them up and burning them.
shots: archive: medieval manuscript illumination death (public domain)

lines.say: Around 1600, Shakespeare's ghosts want justice. Hamlet's father comes back to demand revenge.
Victorian ghosts rap on tables and speak through mediums in dark parlors.
Twentieth-century ghosts show up on film. And now, they're orbs on night-vision cameras and voices in static.
shots: q: night vision camera footage dust orbs

lines.say: Every era's ghosts look like that era's fears and technology. That doesn't prove they're not real. But it's a pattern worth noticing.
shots: line art: ghost outlines changing shape

fact_note: Pliny 7.27 (KNOWN). Medieval revenants, William of Newburgh 12th c. (KNOWN). Hamlet c. 1600 (KNOWN). Victorian séance culture (KNOWN). Orbs explained as flash backscatter from dust (KNOWN). Interpretation of pattern (DEBATED).
ig_caption: roman ghosts wore chains, medieval ghosts were literal corpses, victorian ghosts knocked on tables, ours are dust orbs. we get the ghosts we expect
tt_caption: how ghosts have changed through history #ghosts #history

lines.say: Here's a strange idea about ghosts. What if they aren't spirits at all? What if they're replays?
shots: q: old film projector beam dust

lines.say: Many hauntings look like loops. The same figure, the same staircase, the same time of night. It doesn't notice you. It just repeats.
In the 1960s, a British writer named Tom Lethbridge suggested that places might soak up strong emotions and play them back.
In 1972, the BBC made it a TV drama called The Stone Tape. Ever since, people call it the Stone Tape theory.
The idea is that stone, like magnetic tape, records something from an event, and certain people can sense the playback.
shots: q: reel to reel tape spinning
line art: wall with sound waves inside

lines.say: To be clear: no physics we know of allows stone to record a person. Nobody has measured it.
But it would explain why so many ghosts act less like someone visiting, and more like a scene stuck on repeat.

fact_note: T. C. Lethbridge, 'Ghost and Ghoul' 1961, place-memory idea (KNOWN). Nigel Kneale's 'The Stone Tape', BBC, 1972 (KNOWN). Theory has no physical mechanism (KNOWN). Theory itself is SPECULATION.
ig_caption: not saying I believe it. but the 'ghost on repeat' thing always bugged me and this is the only idea that explains it
tt_caption: the Stone Tape theory, are ghosts just recordings? #ghosts #paranormal
